about.intro: I'm Tiyah, a 23-year-old creative with a passion for art, design and making things that didn't exist before. I've always been someone who loves creating, experimenting with ideas and finding ways to bring the things in my head into the real world. But what I find even more exciting is that my work doesn't have to stop with me. I get to put something I've imagined out into the world for someone else to experience, interact with and hopefully connect with. Whether it's making someone feel something, see things from a different perspective, spark their curiosity or learn something new, I want what I create to leave a little something behind. There's something pretty amazing about knowing that something you made could mean something to someone else.
about.portfolio: Showcase work leads with Clinical Trial, Don't Forget to Say Goodbye, and Bushveld Brothers — each with poster, team credits, brief, synopsis, role, contributions, engine, languages, tech, process, screenshots, demo, and download. Additional games sit in a separate section.
about.file: The work sits across code, design, interface, and the story a player walks through. The skills terminal and the CV record list the study and the tools behind the showcase and additional games.
about.headline: The person behind the pixels

sections.title: A little detour...
sections.copy: My journey into game development wasn't exactly a straight line. I initially pursued a BSc in Biomedicine, spending two years exploring a completely different field before realising I wanted something that allowed me to exercise my creativity alongside my technical interests. I wanted to design, experiment, build and bring ideas to life, which eventually led me to take a leap in a completely different direction.
sections.caption: Player 01

sections.title: Finding my world at Vega
sections.copy: My journey as a game developer began at Vega School, where I discovered just how much could be achieved through the combination of programming, art and design. Each year introduced me to new ways of creating interactive experiences, from developing gameplay mechanics and programming systems to crafting visual identities, immersive environments and meaningful narratives. It was where I began to understand that game development was the perfect intersection of my technical and creative interests.
sections.caption: Vega chapter

sections.title: More than just a game
sections.copy: One of the biggest things I've learnt is that games have the potential to be so much more than entertainment. They can teach, challenge perspectives, spark conversations and create emotional connections. I'm particularly drawn to the idea of creating experiences that leave players with something to think about long after they've put down the controller. Whether through storytelling, gameplay or visual communication, I believe every element of a game has the potential to say something.

sections.title: The best of both worlds
sections.copy: I aspire to grow as a well-rounded game developer, with a particular interest in gameplay programming and C# development alongside UI/UX design and visual development. I'm equally fascinated by the logic behind how a game functions and the creative decisions that shape how it looks, feels and is experienced. I'm drawn to the challenge of taking an idea from its initial concept and visual direction all the way through to a fully functioning, interactive experience. Why choose between the art and the code when I can bring both together?

sections.title: Beyond the screen
sections.copy: When I'm not working on a project, I'm usually finding inspiration in other games, exploring different visual styles, experimenting with creative ideas or getting carried away with a new project. I'm naturally drawn to the little details that give things personality, whether it's an interesting colour palette, a beautifully designed interface or an entire fictional world. I believe inspiration can come from just about anywhere, and I'm always collecting ideas for what I could create next.

skills.label: CODE
skills.title: Gameplay programming
skills.copy: Twelve quests are written in C#. Ten use Unity, two use Windows Forms, and Charmfire uses Unreal Engine 5 with Blueprints.
skills.tools: C# · Unity · Windows Forms · Unreal · Blueprints

skills.label: DESIGN
skills.title: Game design
skills.copy: The quest pages record the rules and goals for Bushveld Brothers, Selkie Song, No Exit, Echo's Lament, and Hive Mind.

skills.label: UI / UX
skills.title: UI and UX
skills.copy: On Bushveld Brothers, Tiyah leads the interface work. On Don't Forget to Say Goodbye, she leads design and art.

skills.label: SYSTEMS
skills.title: Systems
skills.copy: Selkie Song includes a player state machine. Charmfire uses state objects for movement and combat, and strategy objects for bot decisions.

skills.label: STORY
skills.title: Storytelling
skills.copy: Don't Forget to Say Goodbye, Selkie Song, Echo's Lament, and Hive Mind are built around a story the player acts out.

skills.label: TOOLS
skills.title: Tools
skills.copy: The quest pages also use Python, Git, and the engines listed above. This site is the public record of that work.
